meta.title: Animal Hospital anomalies data

sources.label: WatchMeWin - Animal Hospital - FULL GAME + ALL ANOMALIES

notes: This dataset uses 14 rows because Death Ritual and Eyeless each have two distinct choice/action variants in the all-anomalies source.
DuckGaming states that some names are based on appearance and visible in-game text. Public names are normalized for player use, while aliases and source timestamps are kept for review.
Storyline-only entries such as Barney, Ratthew, and Ron from Accounting are excluded until a specific anomaly link is confirmed.
Images are intentionally blank because no clean row-representative screenshots were captured in this pass.

items.name: Camera 1
items.warningSigns: The threat is seen through the camera feed instead of normal room treatment.
items.bestAction: Stay focused on the camera clue and stop treating the moment like a normal patient task.
items.consequence: Ignoring the camera event lets the threat keep advancing through the run.
items.cardSummary: Camera 1 is the first surveillance-style anomaly. It matters because the clue comes from the camera view, not from a patient standing in front of you.

items.name: Camera 2
items.warningSigns: A second abnormal camera moment appears after the first camera event.
items.bestAction: Check the camera feed carefully and react before returning to normal treatment.
items.consequence: Missing the second camera clue can turn the camera sequence into a run-ending threat.
items.cardSummary: Camera 2 is the follow-up surveillance anomaly. Treat it as a separate warning because it appears after the first camera scare.

items.name: Bed Monster
items.warningSigns: The patient bed becomes the center of the threat instead of a normal treatment spot.
items.bestAction: Back away from the bed threat and avoid standing close while the anomaly is active.
items.consequence: Treating the bed like a normal patient station can put the player inside the danger zone.
items.cardSummary: Bed Monster turns a normal treatment bed into the threat. The useful clue is the bed itself changing from safe station to hazard.

items.name: Fire
items.warningSigns: A room hazard starts burning instead of behaving like a normal patient event.
items.bestAction: Move away from the flames and avoid staying in the burning area.
items.consequence: Standing in the fire hazard can punish the player before the shift continues.
items.cardSummary: Fire is a direct room hazard. It is easier to read than a hidden monster because the danger is the burning area itself.

items.name: Slime
items.warningSigns: Slime appears as the abnormal object or surface in the room.
items.bestAction: Keep clear of the slime and avoid walking into the hazard while handling the room.
items.consequence: Touching or ignoring the slime can turn a simple room check into a danger moment.
items.cardSummary: Slime is a floor or room hazard style anomaly. Watch the room surface before rushing back into treatment.

items.name: Eyes
items.warningSigns: Eyes appear where the room or patient should look normal.
items.bestAction: Stop rushing the treatment and respond to the visual clue before moving on.
items.consequence: Overlooking the eyes can leave the player reacting late to the anomaly.
items.cardSummary: Eyes is a visual warning anomaly. It is the kind of threat players can miss if they only focus on the next treatment prompt.

items.name: Tentacles Monster
items.warningSigns: Tentacles appear as the main abnormal shape in the room.
items.bestAction: Keep distance from the tentacles and avoid treating the room like a safe station.
items.consequence: Standing too close to the monster hazard can turn the encounter into a fail state.
items.cardSummary: Tentacles Monster is a body-horror room threat. The tentacles are the warning that the room has stopped being safe.

items.name: Death Ritual: Remove Candles
items.warningSigns: A ritual setup appears with candles that can be removed.
items.bestAction: Remove all candles when you want the intervention path.
items.consequence: Removing the candles changes the ritual outcome instead of letting the patient die.
items.cardSummary: This Death Ritual variant is the active intervention path. The key action is removing every candle before accepting the outcome.

items.name: Death Ritual: Let Patient Die
items.warningSigns: The same candle ritual appears, but the player allows the death outcome.
items.bestAction: Let the ritual finish only when you want to see the death-path outcome.
items.consequence: The patient dies and the ritual path resolves differently from the candle-removal route.
items.cardSummary: This Death Ritual variant is the non-intervention path. It is useful to track separately because the choice changes the outcome.

items.name: Eyeless: Talk
items.warningSigns: An eyeless character appears and can be approached as a dialogue choice.
items.bestAction: Talk to Eyeless when you want the dialogue-path outcome.
items.consequence: Talking triggers one branch of the Eyeless encounter.
items.cardSummary: This Eyeless variant tracks the talk choice. It belongs apart from the ignore route because the player action is different.

items.name: Eyeless: Ignore
items.warningSigns: Eyeless appears, but the player can choose not to talk.
items.bestAction: Ignore Eyeless when you want the alternate no-dialogue outcome.
items.consequence: Ignoring him triggers the alternate Eyeless branch.
items.cardSummary: This Eyeless variant tracks the ignore choice. It is separate because the same encounter can play out differently.

items.name: Black Bunny
items.warningSigns: A dark bunny-like threat appears instead of a normal patient.
items.bestAction: Keep distance and treat the encounter as a chase or threat moment.
items.consequence: Letting the bunny close the gap can force a failure or escape panic.
items.cardSummary: Black Bunny is a hostile creature-style anomaly. It is less about diagnosis and more about recognizing the threat quickly.

items.name: Infector
items.warningSigns: The encounter centers on an infection-style threat instead of normal treatment.
items.bestAction: Avoid direct contact and handle the encounter as a spread or infection hazard.
items.consequence: Getting too close can let the infection threat punish the player or route.
items.cardSummary: Infector is the anomaly to treat as a contact danger. The name points to a threat that spreads or punishes close interaction.

items.name: T-Pose
items.warningSigns: A character or patient appears frozen in an unnatural T-pose.
items.bestAction: Do not ignore the pose change; keep space until the encounter resolves.
items.consequence: Treating the T-pose as harmless can leave the player open to the final threat.
items.cardSummary: T-Pose looks simple at first, but the abnormal pose is the warning. It belongs with the late hostile encounters because players may dismiss it too quickly.
